XXI.|OF THE APOSTLES.|355}}</noinclude>that are among the Gentiles, to depart from Moyses: saying that they ought not to circumcise their children, nor vvalke according to the custome. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=22}}† What is it then? needes must the multitude assemble: for they vvil heare that thou art come. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=23}}† Doe this therfore vvhich vve tel thee, There are vvith vs foure men, that haue a vovve on them. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=24}}† Taking these vnto thee, sanctifie thy self vvith them: and bestovv on them, that they may {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Nu. 6, 18.''}}* shaue their heads: and al shal knovv that the things vvhich they heard of thee, are false: but that thy self also walkest {{sup|‖}} keeping the Law. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=25}}† But concerning them that beleeue of the Gentils, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 15, 20.''}}* vve haue written, decreeing that they should refraine them selues from the immolated to Idols, and bloud, and suffocated, and fornication. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=26}}† Then Paul taking the men vnto him, the next day being purified vvith them entred into the temple, shevving the accomplishment of the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Nu. 6, 13.''}}* daies of the purification, vntil an oblation vvas offered for euery one of them.

{{verse|chapter=21|verse=27}}† But vvhiles the seuen daies were a finishing, those Ievves that vvere of Asia, vvhen they had seen him in the temple, stirred vp al the people, and laid handes vpon him, {{verse|chapter=21|verse=28}}† crying, Ye men of Israël, help: this is the man that against the people & the Law and this place teaching al men euery where, hath also moreouer brought in Gentiles into the temple, and hath violated this holy place. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=29}}† (For they had seen Tróphimus the Ephesian in the citie vvith him, vvhom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.) {{verse|chapter=21|verse=30}}† And the vvhole citie vvas in an vproare: and there vvas made a concourse of the people. And apprehending Paul, they drevve him forth of the temple: and immediatly the doores vvere shut. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=31}}† And as they sought to kil him, it vvas told the Tribune of the band, That al Hierusalem is in a confusion. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=32}}† Vvho forthvvith taking vnto him souldiars & Centurions, ranne downe to them. Who, when they had seen the Tribune and the souldiars, ceased to strike Paul. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=33}}† Then the Tribune comming neere apprehended him, and commaunded him to be bound vvith tvvo chaines: and he demaunded vvho he vvas, and what he had done. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=34}}† And some cried one thing, some an other, in the multitude. And vvhereas he could not knovv the certaintie for the tumult, he commaunded him to be led {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ In castra. ''So in the places folovving''.}}∷ into the castel. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=35}}† And vvhen he vvas come to the staires, it chaunced that he vvas caried of the souldiars because of<noinclude>{{rh||Yy ij|the}}</noinclude>
